$comment: §8 ratification record (resolution plan) — the four decision-maker sign-off points, answered by rvo on 2026-07-28 (AskUserQuestion in the Step-B build session; also recorded in PR #29's body). After this record the freeze applies: any change to a frozen artifact or the measurement surface (bound by frozenSurfaceDigest below, recomputed and enforced by the matrix/fidelity gate) invalidates affected timing data and requires a plan amendment plus one adversarial review round. The matrix (Step C) refuses to run unless this file is committed, all four answers are non-empty, noiseBand equals pilot.json's calibrated band, and the digest matches the working tree.

answers.noiseBandAndDominance: RATIFIED — noise band 1.25 (K=5 pilot of T0 on C2 at the frozen revision: walls 22360/22044/22590/22745/22793 ms, spread 1.034; the formula's floor binds) and §4.7's dominance definition (≥1 unit-win, 0 unit-losses against every eligible rival; within-band differences are ties).
answers.protocolConstants: RATIFIED — K=5; 2 GiB per-unit sampled-peak disk gate; G4 attributable-secondary-signal partition pass/warn/fail at 0/1/≥2; T1 caps (alias 250, query-doc 48 KiB, batch content 1.5 MiB, argv 128 KiB) and the full pinned failure policy (6-attempt total, TIMEOUT-type/pinned-regex + 2×{502,503,504}@≥80%-cap split triggers, split depth ≤2 with ≤4 descendants, breaker at 3 consecutive failed dispatches, REST fallback budget max(20, ceil(10%)) for every driver).
answers.corpusPinning: RATIFIED — the corpus as pinned with recorded verification evidence: C1 prometheus/prometheus ×4 branch units (88.6% shared blob oids best pair; the plan's fastify measured ≤14.2% and was swapped under the amended sharing-measure definition), C2 nestjs/nest (2,128 files, 51 manifests; undici measured 791 files and was swapped), C3 kubernetes/kubernetes (REST tree 37,393 entries, mean path 64.2 B, 21,461 at directory depth ≥6; T2a api-escapes here per the pinned threshold), C4 llvm/llvm-project (REST-truncated at the pin; 1,274 reads via the production clone-walk; oversized-and-truncated → T2a clones anyway, the exhibited hole), C5 PowerShell/PowerShell (measured autocrlf checkout divergence on selected files), C6 = M9 + ansible symlink + git/git non-UTF-8 (single-repo unification exhausted over all three candidates with per-candidate evidence recorded; the split stands per the amended §4.2 contingency) — INCLUDING C3/C4's natural workload sizes and their budget cost.
answers.symlinkPolicy: RATIFIED — REST-dereference parity with today's findings for every driver: mode-120000 entries resolve via the REST dereference fallback (counted against the universal fallback budget); T0 delivers the same dereferenced bytes as its status-quo primary; the canonical link payload stays a latent 2c capability, not a findings change.

amendments.at: Step B, continuation adversarial loop over the audit's un-re-reviewed tail (a NET-NEW three-model loop: Claude Opus 4.6 @ xhigh, GPT-5.5 @ xhigh, GPT-5.6 Sol @ ultra; fresh reviewers each round, cap raised to 5 by the operator)
amendments.why: The post-restack audit closed NOT-CONVERGED with its round-6 fixes, the prose-remediation code fixes, and the CI-flake test fix never seen by any reviewer round, so a follow-on loop ran over the full diff with reviewers directed to weight that tail. Round 1 (verdicts: PASS / PASS / FAIL) confirmed eight findings — every one verified against the code before fixing, none refuted.
amendments.continuationLoopOutcome: CLOSED at the 5-round cap: NOT-CONVERGED. Round verdicts (A: Claude Opus 4.6 @ xhigh, B: GPT-5.5 @ xhigh, C: GPT-5.6 Sol @ ultra, fresh reviewers each round): PASS/PASS/FAIL, PASS/FAIL/FAIL, PASS/PASS/FAIL, PASS/PASS/FAIL, PASS/PASS/FAIL — no unanimous round. A passed all five rounds, B passed four of five (and its one FAIL was confirmed and fixed), C failed all five, each time with genuinely new confirmed findings — a PASS is evidence a reviewer found nothing, never that nothing exists, and C's round-5 findings prove the well was not dry at the cap. 22 findings fixed across five commits (8 + 7 + 3 + 2 + 2, itemised below), 1 refuted with recorded reasons. The round-5 fixes (the unaccepted-2xx record classification and the guarded run-cache DB open) landed after the final round and, as of this amendment, have not been re-reviewed by any further round. The loop's own strictness produced the NINTH transient-becomes-permanent instance (round 4) by over-tightening the ledger rounds 1–3 had loosened in the other direction — the recurring lesson stands: verify each fix against production-realistic inputs in BOTH failure directions.
fixedInContinuationRound1: EIGHTH instance of the transient-failure-becomes-permanent-verdict class: the fidelity battery's T1 branch sent a per-alias TIMEOUT outcome to the closed default (UnitFailure → a durable fidelity-driver-failure marker), although the matrix's frozen table routes exactly that response to REST as timeout-singleton, never a terminal verdict; the battery now takes the same route and hash-verifies the delivered bytes. NOTE ON THE ROUND-5 RECORD: alsoFixedInReviewRound5's first item listed per-alias TIMEOUT among the pass:false leaks its else-rewrite addressed — the rewrite RELOCATED that instance (pass:false row → driver-failure marker) rather than fixing it; it is discharged only now

the §4.5 R2 success ledger's PRODUCER was still unsound after the okRequestClasses rewiring: summarizeTraffic counted a success-shaped GraphQL envelope from a gh that exited nonzero (benchT1's truncated-transfer transition, which the analyzer retries and never accepts) as a successful attempt, minting R2-authorizing evidence from a dispatch the driver itself classified as a transport failure; the ledger now requires exit 0 for GraphQL records (REST already threw truncated-transfer before any ok record could exist)

the fidelity abort/driver-failure MARKER append failure was a swallowed one-line warning while the evidence-row append had been made loud — the round-6 laundering logic applies identically (a lost driver-failure marker lets a later invocation launder a no-rerun verdict; a lost abort marker refunds the spent ≤1 allowance); the failure now prints the marker itself and annotates the propagating abort, which still propagates

the invalidated-finalisation row hardcoded probeDivergences:0 while carrying nonempty probeDivergenceDetails from the verification that runs before the failed accounting read — the count now derives from the same verification as the details and g1/g2 fields on that row

the fidelity marker taxonomy mapped error shapes outside the harness's typed classes to NO marker at all, so an untyped throw (e.g. a synchronous launch failure surfacing straight from the runtime) aborted the battery invisibly and re-invocations were never countable against the ≤1 allowance; classification is now the extracted, CI-driven classifyFidelityAbort, fail-closed: unknown shapes are counted operational aborts. inFlight is also cleared when a (fixture, driver) unit completes, so a post-loop throw (the battery-failure verdict) cannot mint a marker misattributed to the last unit. DELIBERATELY UNTOUCHED: benchSpawn's own error classification — whether spawn-level failures should remain durable driver failures is the recorded-open §4.5 spawn/network-evidence question deferred to the decision-maker

the sole-spawn scan's allowlist entry for scripts/github.ts and its scanner-file exemptions were SUFFIX matches, so a nested file borrowing those names could carry an unscanned launch site or bypass the scan entirely; every entry is now an exact repo-relative path, as the benchSpawn entry already demanded of itself

benchProtocol.test.ts's httpRec fixture let a status-502 record inherit classification:'ok' — a combination benchGh cannot emit — and the ledger logic consumed it; 5xx fixtures now carry 'transient', and the ledger gained direct tests: an exit-nonzero GraphQL 'ok' record mints nothing, an exit-0 one does, a transient 5xx never does

two record paths could carry diskReclaimFailed:true without the operator log the ratified reclaim-failure refutation promises (the drift-restart early return and the invalidated-finalisation throw both bypass the normal tail's log); both now emit the same RECLAMATION FAILED line after their append
fixedInContinuationRound2: the round-1 timeout-route fix exposed the rest of the family: per-alias MISSING and UNATTRIBUTED outcomes still fell to the fidelity closed default (permanent driver-failure markers) although the frozen table routes both to REST as missing-alias-fallback (unattributed after one batch-level retry, which the battery now performs), and a singleton pathless batch-timeout still became an operational abort although the matrix routes it to REST as timeout-singleton; the battery now mirrors all three routes — the REST read's §4.4 pinned-object classifier keeps a dead pin a re-pin condition, never a verdict. This SUPERSEDES the round-6 disclosure that listed batch-timeout among the battery's operational-abort kinds: that treatment predated the route-mirroring principle, and aborting where the frozen table delivers was the same transient-verdict asymmetry in a milder form

one more §4.5 R2 ledger leg: a 200 whose body the envelope parser cannot read produced classifyGraphql 'ok' (empty error list) with exit 0, passing the round-1 exit-code guard while benchT1's '200 non-JSON body' arm treats exactly that dispatch as an http-failure; benchGh now records classification 'malformed-body' for it (non-200 statuses keep their status-based verdict), and a ledger test covers it

under the round-1 fail-closed marker taxonomy, the fidelity fixture-404 RE-PIN throw (a plain Error) would have been counted as a harness-fault operational abort; it now throws the SAME typed RePinRequired the matrix engine classifies as its re-pin-required outcome, and the battery appends NO marker for it — re-running before the re-pin reproduces the condition (nothing to launder) and the §8 amendment changes the digest anyway

the round-1 marker-append annotation mutated the caught Error's message unguarded — a frozen/non-writable Error would have replaced the propagating abort with a TypeError, masking the evidence the annotation exists to preserve; the assignment is now guarded, with the loud marker log as the always-available channel

the round-1 fixture-realism fix was itself unrealistic (the introduce-while-fixing failure mode this file keeps recording): the corrected 502 fixtures inherited exitCode:0 although gh exits 1 BY DESIGN on every non-2xx response; 5xx fixtures now carry exit 1

the RECLAMATION FAILED operator line claimed 'files remain under runDir' although the flag also covers a run-cache DB close failure and dbPath sidecar residue outside runDir; all four log sites now name both locations
cosmetic: the benchSpawn allowlist comment's broken indentation (flagged by reviewer A in both rounds)
fixedInContinuationRound3: one more §4.5 R2 ledger leg: degenerate-but-parseable 200 envelopes ({}, {"data":null}, non-object data, errors:[]) carried classifyGraphql 'ok' (an empty readable-error list) with exit 0 and minted ledger successes while the analyzer routed the dispatch as unattributed/malformed; the record classification is now the extracted, CI-driven graphqlRecordClassification — an 'ok' verdict the envelope cannot support (unparseable body, no data OBJECT, or malformed errors[] evidence) records 'malformed-body'; non-'ok' verdicts pass through with their honest status-based story

the transition table's complete-set rule stopped at the container boundary: a pathless all-TIMEOUT set returned batch-timeout WITHOUT examining attributed errors, so a FORBIDDEN alias error rode a transient batch-timeout verdict into the split/fallback path the closed default exists to deny — the same masking the recorded per-set rule (codex R2 finding 12) removed within each set; batch-timeout now requires every error in BOTH containers to be timeout-typed, and the mixed case takes the closed default

the frozen bench-config carried a fidelityBattery.when:'after-matrix' ordering claim that no code parsed or enforced and the plan never ratified — a frozen config must not claim what nothing checks; the field is REMOVED (not enforced: inventing ordering semantics mid-loop would create un-ratified protocol, and forcing the matrix before fidelity would burn budget on drivers a fidelity G1 already dooms), the $comment states that ordering is deliberately unpinned, and repsPerFixtureDriver is now parsed and gate-validated to exactly 1 (the battery is single-pass by construction; a different pin requires the implementing code change with its §8 amendment)
fixedInContinuationRound4: NINTH instance of the transient-failure-becomes-permanent-verdict class — manufactured by this loop's own strictness direction: rounds 1–3 tightened the §4.5 R2 ledger against FALSE successes, but a production-realistic partial-data 200 (some aliases resolved, one attributed NOT_FOUND — e.g. a pinned workload carrying one dead path on EVERY repetition) is classification 'fatal' on the http record (production drops partial data BY DESIGN) while the frozen T1 table delivers its resolved aliases hash-verified; the ledger therefore NEVER minted graphql-batch for such units, and a later transient 5xx exhaustion was denied its R2 replay and became terminal G3. summarizeTraffic now takes the caller's table-accepted classes as a second ledger source, and the engine passes ['graphql-batch'] when a T1 rep delivered ≥1 alias via the primary route (liveState.routesDelivered, the conservative delivered-content reading of 'succeeded')

the round-2 reclamation-message fix named the sidecar CATEGORY but still interpolated only runDir — an operator chasing cache-DB residue was handed a possibly-already-deleted directory path; all four log sites now print the cache-DB path (with its -wal/-shm sidecars) beside the run directory
fixedInContinuationRound5: one more §4.5 R2 ledger leg, the ledger family's fifth: production's classifier calls ANY errorless 2xx 'ok' (github.ts classifies 200–299 with no readable errors as ok — a proxy-transformed 203/206 included, with gh exiting 0), while benchT1 routes every non-200 status to its closed default; the record therefore minted a graphql-batch ledger success from a dispatch the driver rejects wholesale. graphqlRecordClassification now records 'unaccepted-2xx' for an 'ok' verdict on a non-200 status

AuditDb.open ran BEFORE the try that owns run-resource reclamation: an open that creates the cache DB file and then fails mid-initialisation (WAL/schema setup, ENOSPC) leaked the DB and its -wal/-shm sidecars under the run-cache directory with no reclamation attempt and no path-bearing log (cmdMatrix's outer cleanup removes only benchRoot); the open is now guarded — a mid-initialisation throw sweeps its own debris best-effort and logs the path before rethrowing
refutedInContinuationRound2: treating the http-failure and throttle-retry analysis kinds as ≤1-counted operational aborts in the fidelity battery was flagged as granting retries §4.5 does not permit; REFUTED: the matrix RETRIES exactly those dispatch shapes in-run (requeue under the attempt budget, throttle wait-and-redispatch) without any permanent consequence, so the battery's single counted abort across invocations is strictly TIGHTER than the matrix's own treatment of the same responses, and the breadth is the round-6 disclosed design — the battery has no repetition ledger, so §4.5's R2 predicate cannot apply verbatim

amendments.at: Step B, post-restack adversarial audit (a NET-NEW three-model loop: Claude Opus 4.6 @ xhigh, GPT-5.5 @ xhigh, GPT-5.6 Sol @ ultra; fresh reviewers each round)
amendments.why: The prior remediation loop closed without unanimous approval and its final prose-fix commit was never re-audited, so a fresh full-diff loop ran. Round 1 (verdicts: PASS / FAIL / FAIL) found, and this amendment fixes, two first-order defects among sixteen: (1) the round-5 fix that checked gh's exit code before the T1 transition table was itself wrong — gh exits 1 BY DESIGN on a complete HTTP-200 envelope carrying errors[] and on every non-2xx status (github.ts documents this and deliberately avoids the broad guard), so the guard dead-coded the §4.4 transition table's errored-envelope and non-2xx arms — every nonzero-exit path except the malformed-errors closed default that ran before it (200-with-TIMEOUT never split, RATE_LIMITED never throttled, 502/503/504 never armed the 5xx split trigger, partial data was never accepted); clean exit-0 200 resolution and that one pre-guard default were all that stayed live — the exit code is now failure evidence only for a success-shaped 200 from a failed gh, the original finding's actual case; (2) a SEVENTH instance of the transient-becomes-permanent class: matrix resume terminalized a washed-out unit-failure row even when the frozen §4.5 discipline had mandated an in-slot R1/R2 replay that never landed a record — an interrupt anywhere in the minutes-long replay run silently forfeited the replay, leaving a permanent G3 failure. Resume now reconstructs owed replays with the same evaluated-at-failure-time predicate (ledger restricted to completions before the failed position, so a live no-rerun decision reconstructs identically), and washout markers pair with run rows IN ORDER per position, so an attempt's marker can no longer vouch for its replay's unfinished washout.
fixedInAuditRound1: drift discovered at runtime after a resume restarted only the unfinished SUFFIX of the unit (restored terminal positions shielded pre-drift production-form reps from the epilogue, mixing acquisition forms into one median against §4.4); the unit's positions are now cleared from the terminal set when drift lands

a failed post-run rate-limit read OVERWROTE an already-classified terminal outcome with invalidated-finalisation — a re-pin-required row (which must REFUSE resume) became a row resume silently re-runs against a dead SHA; classified outcomes now keep their record with degraded consumption fields, and only complete runs take the invalidated-finalisation path

the freeze gate's append-only exemption was a raw prefix match, so a stray runs.jsonl.bak or a staged RENAME of an evidence log passed the clean-tree leg; exemptions now match exactly (directories by trailing-slash prefix), rename records always refuse, and the append-only CLAIM itself is verified — committed bytes must be a byte-exact prefix of the working copy

a corrupted runs.jsonl line was silently skipped on resume, which could drop a terminal halt-r5/re-pin row and resume straight past a frozen-assumption breach; it now refuses as freeze-repair territory

the scaffolding lane's argv gate compared the caller-substituted vector against ITSELF (every caller passed the same object as argv and expectArgv), a guard that could never fail; scaffolding argv is now DERIVED inside the launch site from the config-pinned tuple + slots, making the pinned tuple the single source

the primary scored wall accumulated through Date.now(); an NTP step or manual clock adjustment mid-run would stretch, shrink, or negate exactly one driver's wall — WallClock now defaults to a monotonic source

the T1 circuit breaker discarded the last analysis's raw condition (§4.4 requires the raw condition recorded), and a backoff sleep was charged to the scored wall even when the attempt budget was already spent and no retry could follow

pinning's GraphQL probe accepted a Blob-shaped alias WITHOUT checking oid/byteSize identity, so a fact about the wrong object could permanently pin an entry's route (the probe's own test fixture omitted both fields); identity is now validated, and the probe's tighter content cap — which made packBatches throw at pinning for any entry between the probe and matrix caps — is gone (over-matrix-cap entries are excluded outright, since planRounds routes them by size alone)

deriveRoutes consulted the pinned GraphQL facts BEFORE the content-cap size check while planRounds pre-routes by size alone — an over-cap entry GitHub also judges binary would have pinned a route the driver structurally cannot deliver (G2 by construction); size now precedes, and no committed workload changes (none carries an over-cap read entry)

the fidelity battery served gate-relevant reads from the PERSISTENT pinning cache, letting a stale or corrupted local row become a permanent pass/fail verdict with no transport; the battery now runs uncached, and its T2c teardown check no longer REPLACES an in-flight readObject error (the disposal verdict is appended to it instead)

the FINAL disk sample used the tolerant walker, so an unreadable run dir recorded a plausible 0-byte peak with sampleError null (G4-passing by fabrication) — on a short run that sample can be the ONLY one; it is now strict like the clone-store measurement, degrading to sampleError on failure

a fired BatchChild per-read deadline left no durable evidence (the disposal's spawn record hardcoded timedOut:false), spawn records were collected but never written to any run row, and a wedged stream pump let dispose() return a clean-looking verdict while readers stayed attached; the deadline now records as timedOut, every run row carries spawn statistics (total/timeouts/non-zero exits/never-settled, by lane), and a pump-join timeout cancels the readers and surfaces as an unclean disposal
run rows reduced G1/G2/probe-divergence evidence to bare counts (a global §4.7 disqualification was unauditable from the committed log); rows now carry the first 20 of each with counts staying exact

the R5 halt record reported diskReclaimFailed:false although reclamation had not yet been ATTEMPTED on that path; the field is now null there ('not attempted'), and the REST truncated-transfer error now carries its typed classification/request-class evidence

the engine comment claiming the pilot 'honours the same frozen semantics as the matrix' was FALSE — the pilot bounds both R3 and R4 at 2 invalidations per repetition and stops, where the matrix halts on the second R4 per unit and never caps R3; the comment now states the actual divergence and why (a pre-ratification diagnostic surfacing a noisy account early, not the frozen discipline)

deferredWithReasons.instrumentation-failure-consumes-the-rep: a reviewer held that a disk-sampler failure on an otherwise-complete run should invalidate and replay the repetition rather than degrade its disk fields (the row lacks G4 evidence). Degrade-not-eat is the RECORDED design (review-round-2 entry above) and §4.5's frozen replay taxonomy has no category for instrumentation failure — adding one is a plan amendment for the decision-maker, not an audit fix. Step C's scoring must treat diskSampleError rows as missing G4 evidence, not as measurements
deferredWithReasons.typed-harness-evidence-kind: no {kind:'harness'} variant was added: a non-HTTP UnitFailure records {kind:'unit'}, while a generic harness/driver error records failureEvidence null with the 'harness/driver error:' failureCause prefix — the rerun predicate rightly refuses both shapes

fixedInAuditRound2: round-2 verdicts: PASS / FAIL / FAIL. Two of the fixes repair ROUND-1 FIXES (the introduce-while-fixing failure mode this loop's history warns about): (a) round 1's count-based washout-marker pairing created PERMANENT marker debt — an interrupted washout left an orphan unmarked row, and every resume re-ran the position, adding one row and one marker each time, so the deficit never closed and completed measurements were duplicated forever; (b) round 1's append-only prefix verification SKIPPED on any git-show failure, failing open for exactly the rewritten-log case it exists to catch. The root repair replaces both mechanisms: markers now pair with rows by LOG ORDER (a marker certifies the row it follows; at most the final event may be unmarked, anything else refuses), and an interrupted washout is returned as owedWashout for the caller to COMPLETE (sleep + append the marker) — §4.5's separation is idle time, never a reason to re-run an attempt that already measured. Presence-in-HEAD is now probed with `ls-tree HEAD --` (exit 0 + empty output = genuinely absent); any other git failure refuses, as does an in-HEAD log missing from the working tree (deleting an evidence log is not appending). KNOWN LIMIT stated in place: the prefix proof covers committed evidence only — rows appended since the last commit are protected only by committing them

resume rows are now validated against the FROZEN schedule's identity at their position (unit/driver/rep/probe must match; unknown positions and unknown outcomes refuse) — a parseable-but-garbage row could previously terminalize a real scheduled position

a log recording TWO R4 straddles on one unit now REFUSES resume: the live traversal already halted for freeze repair at the second straddle (§4.5), and the old scan collapsed the count into a set and would have silently executed a third attempt

R4/R3 invalidation now applies to unit-failure runs too, superseding the failure (with its cause preserved in the record): §4.5 conditions neither replay on completion, and a failure observed under verified foreign interference or across a reset window is contaminated evidence — recording it as the driver's own permanent failure would let a foreign consumer manufacture G3 ineligibility

the pre-rep drift early-return leaked the pending replay bookkeeping: a dispatched R1/R2 replay that hit drift at its probe left replayOfPos/replayKind armed, so the NEXT unrelated row recorded replayKind r1r2 and resume counted a different unit×driver's ≤1 allowance as spent; the drift record now carries the replay identity it was dispatched under and resets the state, and it appends its washout marker so the row/marker invariant holds

probeGqlFacts now rejects a success-shaped envelope from a gh that exited nonzero — the same truncated-transfer evidence rule the matrix analyzer applies; pinning previously committed ground-truth facts from a transfer it could not vouch for

deriveRoutes' T1 precedence now matches the runtime transition table exactly (isTruncated before isBinary/text-null): a blob GitHub reported as both would have pinned binary-fallback while the driver delivered truncated-blob-fallback — a permanent G2 manufactured from a route-label disagreement over identical REST-fallback bytes (no committed workload carries the conflicting state, so every committed matrix re-derives unchanged)

the fidelity battery now enforces §4.2's own discipline over its append-only log: recorded passes at the current surface are skipped on re-run (idempotence), any recorded pass:false REFUSES outright (a mismatch is never rerunnable — re-running until it passed would launder a permanent G1 verdict), harness-fault aborts append a marker naming the in-flight (fixture, driver), and a second such abort refuses. SCOPE, stated precisely after round 6: the ≤1-abort class covers harness faults (BenchOperationalError, incl. the T1 else-branch's transient transport kinds: http-failure/throttle/batch-timeout) plus R1-shaped REST no-response failures — deliberately broader than the matrix's R1/R2 (the battery has no repetition ledger for R2) — while fatal/closed-default kinds, store corruption, coherence and spawn faults are durable non-rerunnable driver-failure rows; a fixture whose verification carries no usable hash now raises an operational error instead of recording pass:false from a malformed artifact
the matrix gate now requires the ratified noiseBand to POSITIVELY be a finite ratio >= 1 before comparing it to the pilot's — strict equality alone accepted two nulls as a bound band

rate_limit snapshots are validated (object root, nonnegative safe-integer counters) — R3/R4 verdicts and the §4.8 reservation previously rode unvalidated numbers, and a null root escaped as a raw TypeError

the strict final disk measurement now stats the db sidecars strictly too (absent is normal; present-but-unreadable fails the measurement), and the disk worker replies with a routed error when a malformed request still carries a usable seq — an immediate loud failure instead of a 120-second deadline wait
an epoch-vs-monotonic clarifying comment on the engine's now() (ISO stamps and reset arithmetic are epoch; the scored wall never accumulates through it)
fixedInAuditRound3: round-3 verdicts: PASS / FAIL / FAIL. The §4.4 SHA-form classifier's pinned-object probe was labeled rest-meta — a CONSUMING core request §4.8 explicitly reserves — so its own spend was excluded from the harness-owned accounting and read as R3 foreign interference; it now rides its own counted class (rest-classifier)

primary GraphQL exhaustion (RATE_LIMITED with remaining 0) was durably recorded as a graphql-rate-limited SECONDARY signal, so two primary exhaustions could manufacture G4's permanent ≥2 threshold; the signal now carries the same remaining-0 exclusion the REST detector applies

T1 retry timing diverged from the production design it evaluates and inflated its own scored wall: the transient backoff exponent was one-based (first wait 2× production's) and every non-primary throttle slept the fixed 60 s base ON TOP of the bucket horizon benchGh had already armed from Retry-After — the exponent is now zero-based and throttle waits ride the horizon alone (production's lease discipline); the REST layer also slept a full backoff after its FINAL attempt, before throwing exhaustion

pathless GraphQL errors were classified one-by-one in array order, so a recognized TIMEOUT could mask a forbidden sibling the closed default exists to catch (and vice versa, order-dependently); the pathless set is now collected first and must be ALL timeout-shaped to split — anything else is the closed default

alias attribution accepted any path segment shaped like an alias anywhere in the path — [rateLimit, a0] (a different subtree) and [repository, a00] (a name the generator never produces) both attributed to alias 0, misrouting another alias's error; attribution now requires exactly [repository, a<i>] with no leading zeros

present-but-wrong-typed error members (an object-valued message on a TIMEOUT, a numeric type) were sanitized to null and processed, accepting envelopes production's parser marks malformed; they now count as malformed evidence and take the closed default

a reported GraphQL cost below the 1-point accounting floor (§4.6 item 2 imputes 1; §4.8 calls 1 a floor) was accepted verbatim, so a cost:0 reading made the run's own consumption look foreign; sub-floor costs are now treated as unreadable and imputed

§4.4's 'the conflict recorded' was FALSE in implementation — analyzeBatchResponse computed data/errors conflicts and runT1 dropped them, and alias/batch TIMEOUT events that later split-and-succeeded left no durable trace; both now land on every run row (t1Conflicts, t1BodyTimeouts)

resume bound rows to the exact HEAD commit (and the environment hash folded the commit in), so committing the evidence logs — which the round-2 append-only protection itself advises — orphaned every prior row despite an UNCHANGED frozen surface; rows now carry and bind to the §8 content digest, the commit stays stamped as per-row provenance, and the environment hash excludes it

a failure in the PRE-DRIVER phases (live-head probe, WC planning, reservation, the before-snapshot) threw past the outcome classifier: cmdMatrix died with NO row at all and every re-invocation retried the position freely with no evidence trail; those phases now classify into a durable run row exactly like driver failures

an R1/R2 failure recorded by a drifted unit's EPILOGUE was terminalized on resume (the drifted-unit guard suppressed owed-replay reconstruction), forfeiting the mandated replay — the epilogue-failure case is now owed like any other; live drift now also purges the discarded reps' entries from the in-memory success ledger so live and resumed R2 decisions agree

a resumed re-execution of an R3/R4-invalidated position ran UNMARKED (no replayOfPos/replayKind), losing §4.5's physical-predecessor bookkeeping on exactly the crash-resume path; such positions are now dispatched as owed in-slot r3r4 replays. A SECOND invalidated-finalisation at one position now refuses resume (persistent accounting failure must not become an unbounded silent retry class)

pinning's GraphQL probe accepted success-shaped envelopes from a gh that exited nonzero (the matrix analyzer's truncated-transfer rule, unapplied at pin time); the fidelity battery's operational-abort marker fired only for BenchOperationalError, so a BenchHttpError abort (e.g. T0 no-response exhaustion) left re-invocations uncountable against §4.2's ≤1 discipline — the abort whitelist now covers the operational/transport classes

cloneObjectStoreBytes walked all of .git — T2a's checkout builds a full index that T2c's --no-checkout store lacks, a driver-correlated mislabel of §4.6 item 3's object-store metric; it now walks .git/objects, and a post-acquisition failure still measures the store it actually cloned (the acquired dir survives in the live mirror instead of flattening to a null indistinguishable from no-clone)

an immediately-failing REPLACEMENT batch child threw the raw second error past the double-death wrapper, discarding the FIRST child's retained diagnosis (its poisoned condition and git's stderr); both double-death paths now carry it

makeEngine could strand its freshly-created pa-bench-* temp root if any construction step threw (nothing sweeps that prefix, by design); construction now reclaims it on failure, and the entrypoint header states that hard-interrupt-stranded roots are safe to delete. The fidelity battery no longer constructs an entire unused engine (which appended a spurious env-manifest row to runs.jsonl and spent a live GET /user for a temp dir it never used)
fixedInAuditRound4: round-4 verdicts: PASS / FAIL / FAIL. An SSO-enforcement 403 carrying a RATE_LIMITED body was recorded as a graphql-rate-limited SECONDARY signal and RETRIED through the throttle path — a fatal auth condition production fails fast on could both trip the circuit breaker and feed G4's irreversible ≥2 count; fatal classifications now emit no signal, and non-200 fatal classifications take the closed default (round 5 scoped the preempt: fatal-classified 200 envelopes flow through the table)

THE HUMBLING ONE, recorded plainly: round 4's fatal-preempt was itself the table-preemption failure again — production classifies EVERY 200 envelope carrying non-throttle errors[] as fatal (its drop-partial-data design), so preempting on classification alone dead-coded the §4.4 table for exactly the envelopes it attributes, and the round-3/4 table tests stayed green because their fixtures carried classification:'ok', which production NEVER produces for errored envelopes. the mid-unit drift path performed two fallible evidence appends before releasing the live sampler worker (an ENOSPC on either append leaked it); the release now sits in a finally, mirroring the R5 path

an HTTP-200 envelope with a PRESENT-but-EMPTY errors[] parsed as well-formed and could complete a scored run — production's envelope parser rejects an empty errors list (the GraphQL spec requires non-empty); it now counts as malformed and takes the closed default

the fidelity battery's rerun boundary was tightened: round 5's synthetic pinning-time ledger (which granted R2 replays §4.5's prior-completed-repetition predicate cannot support) is gone — a BenchHttpError abort qualifies only via R1's no-response shape — and the T1 else-branch no longer makes fatal/closed-default analysis kinds rerunnable (those are recorded driver failures); transient transport kinds (http-failure/throttle/batch-timeout) remain operational aborts under the ≤1 allowance, a deliberately-disclosed breadth beyond the matrix predicate since the battery has no repetition ledger

a 404 on a SHA-pinned fidelity read now runs the same §4.4 pinned-object classifier the driver path uses — a dead fixture commit is freeze-repair (re-pin), and was previously recorded as a PERMANENT fidelity-driver-failure row

liveState.cloneDir is now mirrored the moment the store EXISTS (inside acquireStore, both forms) — a post-clone coherence failure previously lost the store measurement because the mirror was assigned only after all fallible validation
a fidelity evidence row that cannot be appended (ENOSPC/EACCES) now stops the battery LOUDLY with the row printed — continuing as if recorded would let a later invocation launder an observed mismatch

cmdFidelity acquires the single-writer lock FIRST and holds everything in nested finallys (lock in its own, so a failing temp-root removal cannot strand it) — the round-5 shape leaked the lock and the temp root on every log-refusal path, and ran substantial pre-lock work concurrently with a live matrix; the lock now also covers pin-corpus, diagnostics, pilot, and refresh-evidence (they clone and consume even though they append no evidence rows), and cmdMatrix locks before any pre-work

BatchChild disposal bounds the async stdin end() (a wedged FileSink promise hung T2c's measured wall indefinitely) and now AWAITS the reader cancellations (bounded) after a pump wedge — §3.1's ordered teardown released the permit and deleted the clone with readers still attached
git binary resolution is memoized per PATH — every launch paid a synchronous PATH scan inside exactly the clone drivers' measured walls, where production resolves once at construction

amendments.auditLoopOutcome: SIX rounds, fresh three-model reviewers each round (Claude Opus 4.6 @ xhigh, GPT-5.5 @ xhigh, GPT-5.6 Sol @ ultra). EVERY round returned PASS / FAIL / FAIL — the loop did NOT converge to unanimity within its cap, mirroring the first campaign's loop, which also never reached unanimity. 79 recorded fix items across six commits (counted from the fixedInAuditRound arrays plus the two headline fixes above; some items bundle several reviewer findings), 7 refuted with recorded reasons, 2 deferred to the decision-maker (plus the pre-existing recorded-open finding, whose scope this audit broadened). Reviewer A (Opus) passed every round while the codex reviewers carried all findings — a PASS is evidence a reviewer found nothing, never that nothing exists. The round-6 fixes, and the code the subsequent prose-accuracy audit produced (the okRequestClasses success-ledger wiring — the ledger had granted §4.5 R2 replays from ATTEMPTED request classes rather than classes with ≥1 successful attempt — the diskReclaimFailed operator log, and the re-audited refresh-evidence disclosures), were subsequently re-reviewed by the follow-on continuation loop recorded in the amendment above, which confirmed and fixed further defects in that tail. Three separate times during the two campaigns, a fix for the gh-exit/fatal-classification family itself re-introduced the table-preemption failure it was fixing (rounds R5-of-campaign-1, audit R4, caught finally at audit R5/R6) — the recurring lesson this file keeps recording: verify the fix against PRODUCTION-REALISTIC inputs, not fixtures the fix's author invents.

refutedInAuditRound3.invalidated-replay-refunds-the-allowance: a reviewer read §4.5's 'not charged to the driver allowance' as refunding a spent R1/R2 allowance when the replay itself gets R3/R4-invalidated; the charge is made at DECISION time and the invalidated replay's slot re-executes without a second charge, so the driver receives exactly its one effective rerun — refunding would permit two
refutedInAuditRound3.kill-escalation-process-group: the -pid group kill can ESRCH under Bun (children share the parent's group) and a TERM-ignoring grandchild could outlive the direct kill; the escalation deliberately copies the production spawn shape (the declared design), and Bun exposes no detached-group spawn to do better without redesigning the production path too
refutedInAuditRound3.crash-lost-replay-traffic: an attempt interrupted after dispatch but before its record loses its API consumption from the books; that spend falls OUTSIDE every run's before/after delta window (so it can never flag R3 falsely) and the reservation re-reads live headroom before every run (so it can never overcommit a bucket) — a WAL-style dispatch journal is not warranted by §4.5/§4.8
refutedInAuditRound3.stale-pilot-band-at-the-gate: the gate binding the ratified band to a pilot produced at a pre-remediation revision is RECORDED, disclosed, and deliberate (pilotProvenance below): re-running the pilot at the frozen revision costs live budget and is the decision-maker's call

refutedInAuditRound2.sampler-tick-contention: a reviewer flagged the 1 Hz sampled-peak ticks as wall-contending instrumentation; the 1 Hz cadence is the PREREGISTERED §4.6 item 4 design and the cross-thread residual is explicitly declared in the amended plan text — changing the sampling protocol is a plan amendment, not an audit fix
refutedInAuditRound2.reclaim-failure-keeps-complete: a reviewer wanted a reclamation failure to invalidate the completed run; the run measured and resolved its workload, the failure is durably recorded (diskReclaimFailed:true) and operator-logged (the log line was added when the prose audit found the refutation claimed it before it existed), and §4.5's taxonomy has no invalidation category for teardown-cleanup failure — recorded evidence, not a silent pass
refutedInAuditRound2.clean-exit-after-dispose-deadline: a reviewer wanted a disposal whose exit-wait deadline expired to be unclean even when the child then exits 0 within the escalation window with both pumps settled; the bounded wait exists precisely to tolerate a slow-but-clean exit, and nothing unvouchable remains on that path

amendments.why: A post-ratification review found the harness biased its own primary metric. The §4.6 disk sampler ran a synchronous recursive directory walk on the main thread INSIDE the measured wall, and two further walks sat between the driver's return and wall.stop(). Walk cost scales with entry count, so it taxed checkout-materialising runs (T2a on every unit EXCEPT the api-escaping C3; T0/T1 on the truncated-tree fallback) and barely touched T2c's --no-checkout store — a driver-correlated tax on exactly the axis under test. The §8 pilot could not have surfaced the DRIVER-CORRELATED part: T0-on-C2 creates no checkout, so its run directory stays small and the walk there is cheap — the pilot rows do record sampling (~1.6 MB peaks), so the cost was small, not zero. Fixed by moving the walk to a worker thread and taking the final snapshot with the wall paused (§4.6 items 1 and 4, both amended). This removes the main-thread BLOCKING. It does NOT remove all wall-time interference, because a walk on another thread still competes for CPU and disk bandwidth with the git subprocess under test. Reclamation stays inside the wall on the normal path, unchanged (see the R5 exception noted below).
alsoFixed: the §8 freeze gate trusted `git status --porcelain` without checking its exit code, so a status-specific failure yielded empty stdout and read as a clean tree — the tamper-detection leg failing OPEN

`git rev-parse HEAD` was unchecked and unvalidated, so a failure recorded harnessCommit:"" in every row and reduced the resume guard's revision check to "" !== "", silently merging rows from different harness revisions

the fidelity battery parsed `ls-tree` output without checking its exit code; the deadline path returns empty stdout, which parsed as 'entry absent from the live tree' and wrote a pass:false row — manufacturing a permanent, never-rerunnable driver disqualification (§4.7) from a transient local failure. Local tooling faults now raise a typed BenchOperationalError instead

pinning coerced an absent, opaque, or alias-errored GraphQL response into the positive fact isBinary:true, which deriveRoutes freezes as primary binary-fallback with no permitted alternative — a latent re-pin hazard that would disqualify T1 on an artifact of one flaky alias. Facts now commit per batch, only when every alias is sound

the mid-unit drift restart returned before teardown, leaking the run's sqlite handle and sidecars while its record claimed diskReclaimFailed:false; reclamation is now idempotent and owned by an outer finally that also covers the pre-driver throw paths. NOTE the R5 exception: that path stops the wall before the halt record is appended, so its reclamation happens in the outer finally OUTSIDE the stopped wall — §4.6 item 1's in-wall reclamation applies to the normal path (citation corrected by the post-restack prose audit — the plan has numbered items, not subsections)

the R5 halt record summed httpBodyBytes without the rest-meta exclusion the normal record applies (contradicting an invariant the module states twice), hardcoded diskSamples:0, and zeroed traffic it had actually observed; both records now derive from one summarizeTraffic helper
buildEnvManifest ignored the exit codes of `git --version` and `gh --version`, so a blank version could enter the environment-manifest hash that binds every timed row

BatchChild.dispose()'s verdict — the fatal condition plus git's retained stderr — was discarded by every caller, so a poisoned teardown could accompany a reported success and the double-death message lost the first child's diagnosis
alsoFixedInReviewRound2: the frozen-surface digest walked scripts/ NON-recursively, silently omitting all eight tracked non-test modules under scripts/tui/ — a freeze that covered less than its own description claimed. The traversal is now recursive, which is why the digest differs from the one first recorded for this amendment

the worker-backed disk sampler had no error channel, no reply deadline, and no idempotence, so a worker that died or never replied would hang between the driver returning and the run record being appended; instrumentation failure now degrades the disk fields (cloneObjectStoreBytes null, diskSampleError set) and never eats the row, which also restores R5's before-any-fallible-work guarantee
cloneObjectStoreBytes was computed with the deliberately-tolerant sampling walker, so an unreadable object store could report a plausible 0 — it is a measurement, so a failed walk is now null
parseProbeBatch accepted arrays and non-Blob nodes and coerced absent fields into definite facts; it now requires __typename Blob with correctly-typed fields

BatchChild disposal was only rejected on an explicit protocol fault, and the fidelity path discarded the verdict entirely; the FINAL successful-path disposal in runT2c and the fidelity disposal now both require exit 0 with no fault. SCOPE: the first child's disposal on the respawn path is captured for diagnostics and is NOT itself gated — a replacement child that succeeds still yields a successful run.
alsoFixedInReviewRound3: the round-2 entry above claimed cloneObjectStoreBytes failures became null; that claim was PREMATURE. The wrapper caught throws, but the walker underneath was still the tolerant duBytes, which returns 0 and never throws — so the catch was unreachable and a missing store still recorded a plausible 0. All three reviewers reproduced it independently. There is now a genuinely strict walker (duBytesStrict) that raises on any unreadable entry, selected per-request so sampled peaks stay tolerant and the recorded measurement does not (the post-restack audit later made the FINAL point sample — which folds into the peak and may be a short run's only sample — strict as well; tick samples remain tolerant; see fixedInAuditRound1/2)
the worker's inbound request was cast rather than validated, and reply sequence numbers accepted fractional/negative values; both are now parsed and rejected

concurrent finish() calls raced through one worker — the first terminated it and cleared the second's pending entry without rejecting it. finish() is now single-flight: the in-progress promise is stored before the first await
the awaited walk's deadline timer was unref'd, so a worker terminated mid-finish could let the process exit 0 with no snapshot and no run row; it is now referenced for the life of the request

pilot.json was READ by the freeze gate but excluded from the digest, so its walls, spread, reps, driver, or slot could be edited freely as long as noiseBand still matched. It is now inside the frozen artifact set
diskSampleError was write-only: nothing logged or acted on it, so a degraded disk row could later read as a real measurement. It now emits an explicit operator warning naming the affected row
runT2c's exception path assigned the disposal verdict in its finally and then skipped the check, discarding the diagnosis exactly as before; an unclean teardown now annotates the propagating error
alsoFixedInReviewRound4: the R5 halt path peeked the sampler and threw without ever releasing it — finish() is the only other disposer and that path deliberately never calls it, so the tick timer stayed armed and the worker outlived the run. A synchronous, infallible, idempotent abandon() now runs immediately after the row is durable

the runT2c exception-path teardown annotation was written to Error.message, but the engine records UnitFailure.cause2 — so the disposal diagnosis was preserved in a field nothing reads and remained absent from runs.jsonl. UnitFailure now exposes annotateTeardown(), which updates cause2 (and keeps message consistent)

the T1 fidelity path mapped an http-failure analysis (5xx / no HTTP response / non-JSON body — the first two transient-classified; a 200 non-JSON deliberately records non-json, outside R2) to route 'unresolved:http-failure' and appended a pass:false row, manufacturing a permanent never-rerunnable driver disqualification from a transport blip. This is the third instance of that defect class found in this harness; it now raises BenchOperationalError like the ls-tree path
amendments.note: The four §8 sign-off answers below are untouched and remain as rvo recorded them on 2026-07-28. This amendment changes the measurement surface, not the decisions: the noise band, protocol constants, corpus pinning, and symlink policy are all unaffected. No timed matrix data existed to invalidate — the matrix has never run.
amendments.reaffirmation: NOT gate-enforced, and deliberately so: the matrix gate checks the digest, not who approved it, so updating frozenSurfaceDigest above is sufficient to let Step C run. The decision-maker should nevertheless re-affirm this amended surface before executing the matrix; that judgement is recorded here rather than mechanised, and no field in this file is checked for it.
alsoFixedInReviewRound5: FOURTH and FIFTH instances of the transient-failure-becomes-permanent-verdict class. The T1 fidelity path routed only http-failure to an operational error; GraphQL TIMEOUT (batch or per-alias), throttle-retry, and the closed default still fell through to route 'unresolved:*' and appended pass:false, disqualifying the driver globally. That branch is now an ELSE — anything that is not one of the delivering cases fails closed, so a NEW analysis kind cannot reopen the hole

analyzeBatchResponse ignored `gh`'s exit code entirely, so a subprocess that FAILED but emitted a parseable 200-shaped body produced resolved aliases — content accepted from a call that did not succeed. A non-zero exit is now an http-failure before any body inspection (SUPERSEDED by the post-restack audit: that broad guard itself dead-coded the §4.4 transition table, because gh exits 1 BY DESIGN on errored 200 envelopes — see fixedInAuditRound1; the exit code is now evidence only for a success-shaped 200 from a failed gh)

runT2c swallowed a REJECTED dispose(): the catch set finalDisposal = null, which the post-teardown check reads as 'nothing to complain about', so a teardown that failed outright returned a clean run. A rejection is now its own unclean verdict on both the success and exception paths
the R5 sampler release ran AFTER runsLog.append, so an appendFileSync failure (disk full, EACCES) left the sampler armed with no disposer remaining; abandon() now runs in a finally around the append

WorkerDiskSampler folded ANY well-shaped reply with an unrecognised sequence into the peak as 'an unawaited tick', so a duplicate, stale, or unsolicited message could fabricate a disk figure the filesystem never held. Exactly one outstanding tick sequence is now tracked and anything else fails the sampler

a throw in post-run finalisation (the rate-limit read) between reclamation and the append discarded a run that had already been measured — wall, traffic and all. It now appends an 'invalidated-finalisation' row preserving the measured wall and partial traffic, marked unscoreable rather than dropped
alsoFixedInReviewRound6: abandon() cleared the pending map without settling it. Because the awaited walk's deadline timers are deliberately REFERENCED (so a dead worker cannot let the process exit mid-measurement), dropping them unsettled left those timers holding the event loop. abandon() now rejects every pending request
the worker's request validator used extras.some(), which SKIPS array holes, so a sparse array passed and was then cast to string[]

GET /user was cast to {login?:string} with a `?? "unknown"` fallback, so a malformed payload silently became the literal identity "unknown" — which then hashes into the §8 environment manifest that every timed row binds to. It is now validated and refuses

openAndDeliberatelyNotFixed.finding: Any git-transport failure — a spawn TIMEOUT (exit 124) OR a prompt network failure (DNS/TLS/connect/reset, typically exit 128, on clone, scaffolding fetch, or the ls-remote probe) — is thrown as UnitFailure with no HTTP evidence, so the engine records failureEvidence {kind:'unit'} and the matrix rerun predicate (evidenceIsRerunnable, benchContentTransport.ts) refuses it: it accepts only {kind:'http'}. A transient transport failure therefore becomes a permanent, non-rerunnable unit failure — the sixth instance of the transient-becomes-permanent class found in this harness. (SCOPE BROADENED by the post-restack audit: the entry originally described only the timeout subset; the prompt network-error subset is the SAME hole — §4.5's R1 names 'DNS/TLS/connect/reset' as its own examples — and understating a recorded-open defect is itself the kind of false claim this file exists to prevent.)
openAndDeliberatelyNotFixed.CORRECTION: An earlier version of this entry claimed the fix was blocked because '§4.5's R1/R2 rerun predicate and the failure policy are covered by ratified answer 2'. THAT WAS FALSE, and the prose audit caught it. Ratified answer 2 covers 'K=5, the 2 GiB per-unit disk gate, the G4 secondary-limit threshold, and the fixed T1 caps and failure-policy CONSTANTS (§4.4)'. R1/R2 is a separate §4.5 completion-discipline definition and is NOT one of the four ratified answers. The reason given for deferring was wrong, and it is recorded here rather than silently replaced because a false justification for NOT doing work is worse than the omission it excused.
openAndDeliberatelyNotFixed.actualStatus: Fixing this is a §4.5 PLAN AMENDMENT of exactly the same kind as the §4.6 amendments already made in this remediation — not a change to any ratified answer. It is deferred only because the adversarial review loop that would validate it has just run five rounds and closed; introducing an unreviewed change to the rerun predicate now would reintroduce the risk that loop exists to manage. Three of those five rounds found defects introduced while fixing the previous round's.
openAndDeliberatelyNotFixed.recommendedFix: Add a typed {kind:'spawn', timedOut:boolean, op:'clone'|'fetch'|'ls-remote'|'ls-tree'} failureEvidence variant carrying BenchGitResult.timedOut and exitCode, PRESERVING WHICH OPERATION FAILED AND HOW, and admit only the network-facing subset in evidenceIsRerunnable alongside R1's no-response case: clone/fetch/ls-remote failures (timeout or prompt network error) plausibly satisfy R1's 'network-layer error outside any HTTP response'; an ls-tree failure is a purely LOCAL operation and does not, and a process-level timeout does not by itself prove which phase stalled. The amendment must therefore either preserve the operation and admit only the network-facing subset, or explicitly broaden R1 to cover local tooling stalls — an earlier draft of this entry recommended admitting all spawn timeouts, which would have over-broadened R1.

harnessCommit: informational only — the digest above is the binding, and each row in runs.jsonl records the commit that produced it. Pre-rebase hashes recorded earlier (e.g. 42c970f) are not ancestors of the current branch.

The pilot + pinning ran under gh login sondrateconsulting-ryan; §4.8's dedicated-otherwise-idle identity requirement for the matrix stands (a foreign single-point GraphQL consumption was live-detected and R3-invalidated during pilot rework — the requirement is not theoretical).

pilotProvenance: The K=5 pilot rows in runs.jsonl were produced at pre-rebase harness revisions (22b7152 / 8e8eb6d), BEFORE the post-ratification remediation changed measurement behaviour. The gate binds the ratified band to pilot.json's band and the surface to the digest; it does NOT bind the pilot rows to the frozen revision. The pilot configuration (T0 on C2) materialises no checkout, so the disk-sampler bias the remediation removed was ~0 there and the 1.034 spread is not expected to move — but that is an argument, NOT a measurement on the current surface. Treat 'the noise band is unaffected' as reasoned, not verified. Re-running the pilot at the frozen revision before Step C would settle it.
